content.intro: This lesson focuses on reading and writing json in applications and connects the PDF syllabus topics to a small, inspectable example. Work from the intended data model, write down the expected result, then verify syntax and semantics with the target tool.
content.why_it_matters: Reading and Writing JSON in Applications matters because structured-data files sit between people, tools, services, and deployment systems. A clear contract and repeatable checks make the result easier to maintain and safer to consume.

content_blocks.title: The core idea
content_blocks.text: Parsing transforms text into values; serialization turns values back into text. File tools, query languages, streaming patterns, and structural comparison each solve different problems, so choose tooling based on input size and intended operation.

content_blocks.title: What you will cover

Handling malformed data.; Choosing encodings explicitly. Separating file I/O from data processing.. Treat each as part of a workflow: define what the data should mean, represent it consistently, and test how the chosen implementation interprets it.

content_blocks.title: Inspectable example: Reading and Writing JSON in Applications
content_blocks.code:
import json
from pathlib import Path

source = Path("input.json")
target = Path("output.json")
data = json.loads(source.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
target.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")
content_blocks.expected_output: With a valid input.json, the script reads the document, parses it, and writes formatted output.json. File I/O errors and malformed JSON still need application-specific handling.

common_mistakes.problem: Treating readable text as proof of correctness.
common_mistakes.why: Syntax and visual formatting cannot establish data types, schema conformance, or application-specific meaning.
common_mistakes.fix: Parse, validate against the intended contract, and test a valid plus an invalid fixture.

common_mistakes.problem: Assuming every parser interprets the feature identically.
common_mistakes.why: Format versions, schema choices, library defaults, and product-specific restrictions affect behavior.
common_mistakes.fix: Record the exact parser/version and test the target environment.

common_mistakes.why: Missing fields, wrong types, duplicate keys, or ambiguous scalars may still break consumers.
common_mistakes.fix: Keep valid, invalid, and boundary fixtures in version control.
